chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Ḥakam ibn Ḥukaym al-Ṣayrafī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I urinate and do not find water, and some urine has touched my hand, so I wipe it on the wall or the dust; then my hand perspires, and I touch my face or some of my body, or it reaches my garment.
He عليه السلام said: “There is no problem in it.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem in it; it is not objectionable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if urine touches the hand, it is wiped on dust or a wall, and then sweat transfers to the body or clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling related to najasah and ritual purity when water is unavailable. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no problem if a hand affected in this manner later perspires and touches the body or garment after being wiped on a wall or dust.
